text_blocks.snippet: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive condition where the kidneys lose their ability to filter waste and excess fluid from the blood. The most common causes of CKD are diabetes and high blood pressure, both of which can damage the delicate blood vessels and filtering units within the kidneys over time. Other contributing factors include heart disease, certain genetic conditions, autoimmune diseases, and urinary tract issues.
